lines.text: A neatly dressed man with an easy manner comes out to greet me before I've even finished parking.

lines.speaker: Robert
lines.text: Welcome, welcome! Not every day a man's car breaks down right in front of a motel. Lucky, in the unluckiest way possible.

lines.speaker: Gabe
lines.text: I need a room for the night.

lines.speaker: Robert
lines.text: Of course. I'll give you room 4, it's the quietest one. If you need anything, any hour, my door's the first one by the lobby.
The kind of efficient manager you'd hope to find out on the highway. He clearly takes care of the place.

lines.speaker: Robert
lines.text: A terrible business, last night, detective. The Starlight has always been a peaceful place. I already spoke with the sheriff first thing this morning.

lines.speaker: Gabe
lines.text: Did you notice anything unusual before the crime?

lines.speaker: Robert
lines.text: There's been a lot of drifters wandering the highway lately. That vagrant, Mark, hangs around the gas station and gets aggressive when he's been drinking. And there's truckers passing through too.
Makes sense. A crime on his property is a death blow for the motel; it's logical he'd want this cleared up fast.

lines.speaker: Gabe
lines.text: I understand the building has a basement. What do you keep down there?

lines.speaker: Robert
lines.text: The machine room: backup generator, boilers, heavy tools. It's damp and poorly ventilated, that's why I keep it locked.

lines.speaker: Robert
lines.text: Why do you ask, detective? If you need to inspect the motel's facilities, I'll gladly walk you through later.
A practical, professional answer. If he's hiding something, he covers it with the calm of a man used to the routine of upkeep.

lines.speaker: Gabe
lines.text: Back to the basement: Elena told me you keep the only key to that door.

lines.speaker: Robert
lines.text: Of course. The boilers are old and the liability insurance is very strict. I can't have inexperienced staff going down there fiddling with valves.
Impeccable, from a business-management standpoint. I'll need hard physical evidence if I want to prove that basement is hiding something more.

lines.speaker: Gabe
lines.text: Elena told me you're the only one with a key to the basement.

lines.speaker: Robert
lines.text: That's right. I handle the boilers and the parts myself to avoid accidents. Basic safety protocol.
The explanation sounds reasonable and measured.

topics.displayName: Confront him with the motel evidence

lines.speaker: Gabe
lines.text: The padlock busted from the inside. Exclusive access, yours alone. And Carla's belongings hidden behind the generator crates.

lines.speaker: Robert
lines.text: Those are very serious inferences, detective. Someone could have forced the lock, or planted those things there to incriminate management.
For the first time, his smile disappears. He keeps his composure, but his eyes weigh every word of mine with cold calculation.

lines.speaker: Robert
lines.text: If you have a formal accusation, I suggest you bring it to the sheriff with all the rigor the law demands.

lines.speaker: Gabe
lines.text: The padlock was busted from the inside, and you're the only one with a key.

lines.speaker: Robert
lines.text: Unfortunate coincidences, detective. But in a serious investigation, coincidences don't add up to a verdict.
He takes a measured second before answering. His defenses are solid, but the physical facts don't lie.
